protocol.instrument_name: NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for the Continuation of Hormonal Contraception
protocol.legal_basis: Not explicitly stated as a regulation or poisons schedule provision. The document states Approved Medicines 'are listed in the NSW Health Authority (25 February 2026)' and is 'Approved Dr Kerry Chant AO PSM, Chief Health Officer and Deputy Secretary, Population and Public Health, 25 February 2026'.
protocol.supervision_model: appropriately trained authorised pharmacists: 'Pharmacists must hold general registration under the Health Practitioner Regulation National Law and have successfully completed the training requirements detailed in the NSW Health Authority (dated 25 February 2026).' Continuation/resupply only - 'pharmacists are not permitted to initiate or change therapy'. DMPA administration additionally requires 'pharmacists successfully completing the Pharmaceutical Society of Australia (PSA) Administering Medicines by Injection Course'.
protocol.scope_summary: Practice standard governing the Community Pharmacy Hormonal Contraception Continuation (Resupply) Service in NSW: authorised pharmacists may supply continuation (resupply) of listed approved hormonal contraceptive formulations - single or combined oral forms, injectable medroxyprogesterone, and the combined intravaginal ring - to eligible patients already established on therapy, with patient assessment, blood pressure monitoring, consent, documentation, counselling and referral requirements. Not a treatment-initiation protocol.

inclusion.text: Continuation of the patient's current hormonal contraception that has been prescribed primarily for the purpose of contraception (service-wide requirement).

The patient has been reviewed by their treating medical practitioner or health service for the purposes of contraception within the last 2 years for the OCP and vaginal ring, or the last year for DMPA.
Therapy is continuation only - 'pharmacists are not permitted to initiate or change therapy'.
'Pharmacists must only provide continuation of formulations listed in the Authority.'
'Patients must be physically present in the pharmacy to be eligible for continuation of hormonal contraception.'
'Patients are required to have a pharmacist consultation, including blood pressure monitoring, before a hormonal contraceptive method may be resupplied.'

Pharmacist requirement: 'Pharmacists must hold general registration under the Health Practitioner Regulation National Law and have successfully completed the training requirements detailed in the NSW Health Authority (dated 25 February 2026).'
DMPA-specific: 'Continuation of DMPA under this service is permitted for patients aged 25 to 39 years old (inclusive) only.'
DMPA-specific: 'Continuation of DMPA under this service is permitted for up to 12-months only. Patients require GP reassessment after this period.'

DMPA-specific: 'DMPA injection must only be administered by pharmacists successfully completing the PSA Administering Medicines by Injection Course. Otherwise, the patient needs to be referred to their GP or relevant health service for deep IM administration.'

exclusion.text: 'patients with a UKMEC category 3 or 4 condition are not eligible for continuation and require a referral' (e.g. migraine with aura, listed as a contraindication to hormonal contraception).

Vaping with nicotine is considered equivalent to cigarette smoking in relation to the MEC: 'any vaping in those aged 35 years and older will be MEC 4 (i.e. absolutely contraindicated) for use of combined hormonal contraception' (combined OCP and vaginal ring).
'There is an increased risk of using combined hormonal contraception (combined OCP and vaginal ring) in smokers over 35 years or those who have quit smoking over the last year.'
'Women over 35 who smoke should be advised to stop combined hormonal contraception as the risk of mortality associated with smoking becomes clinically significant at this point.'
'Women over 50, should be advised to no longer use combined hormonal contraception as there are safer methods of contraception at this stage.'

Pregnancy not excluded: 'if the patient has not been using the method reliably and consistently and has had unprotected sex, then there is a risk of pregnancy. Pharmacists should take all reasonable steps and assessment to exclude pregnancy before continuation of hormonal contraception. Otherwise, the patient should be referred to a medical practitioner (or other authorised prescribing health practitioner) for assessment, pregnancy testing, and advice regarding ongoing contraception.'
'Vaginal ring: Patients needing assistance with insertion must be referred to a medical practitioner or health service.'

'Pharmacists must not assist with physical insertion of a combined hormonal vaginal ring.' Patients requiring assistance with insertion, reinsertion, troubleshooting of placement, or clinical assessment related to discomfort, expulsion, pain, abnormal bleeding, suspected infection, or any concern about correct placement must be referred to their GP or another appropriate health provider.

exclusion_exceptions.text: 'All patients seeking contraception who have not had a cervical screening test (CST) in the previous 5 years should be advised to see a medical practitioner for a CST, and a referral provided if the patient consents. They are still eligible for the Community Pharmacy Hormonal Contraception Continuation service.'

'Despite a natural decline in fertility, women over 40 require ongoing contraception until they reach menopause if they wish to avoid unplanned pregnancy.' (i.e. age over 40 is not itself an exclusion from ongoing contraception.)

diagnosis_pathways.name: Community Pharmacy Hormonal Contraception Continuation (Resupply) - patient assessment and supply pathway

steps.description: Confirm service eligibility before assessment: patient must be physically present in the pharmacy; the current hormonal contraception must have been prescribed primarily for the purpose of contraception; the formulation must be listed in the Approved Medicines (NSW Health Authority, 25 February 2026); the patient must have been reviewed by their treating medical practitioner or health service for contraception within the last 2 years (OCP and vaginal ring) or the last year (DMPA); pharmacists are not permitted to initiate or change therapy. 'Patients who have requested the service but are not eligible for continuation should be referred to their regular medical practitioner or health service.'

gates.criterion: Patient is physically present in the pharmacy
Current hormonal contraception prescribed primarily for the purpose of contraception
Formulation listed in the Approved Medicines (NSW Health Authority, 25 February 2026)
Reviewed by treating medical practitioner or health service for contraception within the last 2 years (OCP and vaginal ring) or the last year (DMPA)
Request is continuation only (no initiation or change of therapy)

steps.description: Obtain informed clinical and financial consent: 'Informed clinical and financial consent must be obtained from the patient prior to providing care under these Practice Standards.' Also seek consent to share a record of the consultation (including adverse events) with the patient's usual treating medical practitioner or medical practice, where the patient has one.

gates.criterion: Informed clinical and financial consent obtained prior to providing care

steps.description: Patient history tailored to the patient's presentation ('The prompts provided below are not exhaustive, pharmacists should maintain an open mind and be aware of cognitive bias'). Include: Age; Pregnancy and breastfeeding status; Underlying medical conditions, including new or recently diagnosed medical conditions (see UKMEC 3 and 4); Current medications, including adherence and satisfaction, and whether use of hormonal contraception has been continuous; Drug allergies/adverse effects; Prior use of contraceptives, tolerability, and adverse effects; Smoking status, including vaping; Any unexplained and un-investigated vaginal bleeding or acute, severe menstrual bleeding; Any headaches indicative of migraines; Last Cervical Screening Test and Breast check; HPV vaccination status. Review My Health Record where appropriate and available.

gates.criterion: No UKMEC category 3 or 4 condition present (e.g. migraine with aura) - 'patients with a UKMEC category 3 or 4 condition are not eligible for continuation and require a referral'
Sufficient information obtained from the patient to assess the safety and appropriateness of continuation

Use of hormonal contraception has been continuous (if a patient frequently takes pill breaks, use professional judgement and consider referring to explore alternative contraception options e.g. LARCs)

steps.description: Sexual and social history and STI screening consideration: consider a brief sexual history to inform shared decision making and assess appropriateness of continuation (previous use and experiences with contraception, current relationship status, risk factors for STIs, including any known STI history of current and/or recent partner). STI screening is recommended for anyone who is sexually active and engaging in unprotected sex, has a new partner since their last STI test, or thinks they may be at risk; recommend STI testing for individuals who may be at risk even if asymptomatic. Note presence of genitourinary symptoms that might suggest a STI: changes in vaginal or urethral discharge; vulval, genital skin problems or symptoms; lower abdominal pain; dysuria. Consider the STI Testing Guideline for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander People for priority populations.

gates.criterion: No genitourinary symptoms that might suggest a STI (changes in vaginal or urethral discharge; vulval, genital skin problems or symptoms; lower abdominal pain; dysuria)
Patient not at increased risk of HIV and other STIs

steps.description: Examination: 'The pharmacist should measure blood pressure (BP) for all patients, and the patient's height and weight to calculate BMI (for patients requesting continuation of the combined hormonal OCP, vaginal ring and DMPA) to determine the patient's suitability for continuing their hormonal contraceptive and record this information in their clinical software program.' A single elevated BP reading is not enough to classify an individual as hypertensive (activity immediately prior to consultation should also be taken into consideration) and a second BP reading should be taken at the end of the consultation. If BP remains elevated, the patient should be referred to a medical practitioner or health service for further assessment and selection of an appropriate contraceptive method. BP should be monitored and recorded every 12 months. BMI should be calculated on the first presentation, and professional judgement exercised regarding whether BMI needs to be recalculated on subsequent presentations.

gates.criterion: Second BP reading at the end of the consultation is not elevated (i.e. BP does not remain elevated)
BP measured for all patients; height and weight measured to calculate BMI for combined hormonal OCP, vaginal ring and DMPA continuation

steps.description: Exclude pregnancy before continuation: 'If the patient has been using the hormonal contraception consistently and reliably, they can be reasonably assumed not to be pregnant.' If the patient has not been using the method reliably and consistently and has had unprotected sex, there is a risk of pregnancy; pharmacists should take all reasonable steps and assessment to exclude pregnancy before continuation, otherwise refer the patient to a medical practitioner (or other authorised prescribing health practitioner) for assessment, pregnancy testing, and advice regarding ongoing contraception. Note that pregnancy tests can give a false negative result if unprotected sex was less than 21 days earlier.

gates.criterion: Patient using hormonal contraception consistently and reliably (reasonably assumed not pregnant)
Pregnancy excluded by all reasonable steps and assessment before continuation

steps.description: Supply continuation (resupply) of an Approved Medicine formulation listed in the Authority (NSW Health Authority, 25 February 2026): single or combined oral forms of ethinylestadiol (35 g or less), levonorgestrel, norethisterone, drospirenone, nomegestrol, desogestrel, dienogest, gestodene; injectable form of medroxyprogesterone (150mg/mL); combined intravaginal form of ethinylestradiol+etonogestrel (2.7+11.7 mg) ring. Formulations, brand examples and doses as printed in Table 1: Formulations approved as part of the continuation service. Pharmacists can provide continuation up to 12-months of the patient's current hormonal contraception (footnote: for patients aged 40-49 pharmacists can only provide one original manufacturer's pack - only one resupply is allowed before the patient will need to be reviewed by their GP or other authorising prescribing healthcare practitioner).

gates.criterion: Pharmacist consultation, including blood pressure monitoring, completed before a hormonal contraceptive method may be resupplied
Continuation within 12-months of the patient's current hormonal contraception (one original manufacturer's pack only for patients aged 40-49)

steps.description: DMPA (depot medroxyprogesterone acetate) continuation branch: continuation permitted for patients aged 25 to 39 years old (inclusive) only; continuation permitted for up to 12-months only; patients require GP reassessment after this period. 'DMPA injection must only be administered by pharmacists successfully completing the PSA Administering Medicines by Injection Course. Otherwise, the patient needs to be referred to their GP or relevant health service for deep IM administration.' DMPA is associated with a reduction in bone mineral density (BMD) during use, which usually recovers after discontinuation; women using DMPA should be reviewed every 2 years by their medical practitioner or health service (RANZCOG), with annual review for osteoporosis and cardiovascular risk factors (Therapeutic Guidelines). Use of DMPA by perimenopausal women needs to be reviewed by a medical practitioner or health service.

gates.criterion: Patient aged 25 to 39 years old (inclusive)
Continuation of DMPA within 12-months (GP reassessment required after this period)
Administering pharmacist successfully completed the PSA Administering Medicines by Injection Course
Patient is not perimenopausal, or perimenopausal use has been reviewed by a medical practitioner or health service

steps.description: Combined hormonal vaginal ring continuation branch: 'Pharmacists must not assist with physical insertion of a combined hormonal vaginal ring.' Patients requiring assistance with insertion, reinsertion, troubleshooting of placement, or clinical assessment related to discomfort, expulsion, pain, abnormal bleeding, suspected infection, or any concern about correct placement must be referred to their GP or another appropriate health provider (also: patients needing assistance with insertion must be referred to a medical practitioner or health service). The ring 'works in the same way as combined oral hormonal contraception and is treated similarly in terms of contraindications, complications, side effects and most drug interactions'; may be a useful option when a combined hormonal contraceptive is desired but non-oral option is preferred (e.g. malabsorptive conditions).

gates.criterion: Patient does not require assistance with insertion, reinsertion, troubleshooting of placement, or clinical assessment related to discomfort, expulsion, pain, abnormal bleeding, suspected infection, or any concern about correct placement
Pharmacist does not attempt physical insertion of the ring

steps.description: Counselling and women's health advice: comprehensive advice and counselling (including supporting written information when required) as per the Therapeutic Guidelines, Australian Medicines Handbook, UKMEC and other relevant resources - Consumer Medicines Information and/or handouts endorsed by relevant organisations; appropriate counselling on the hormonal contraception supplied (how to take, side effects to expect/how to manage, when the hormonal contraceptive is less effective, what to do in the event of a missed pill/late injection/late insertion of next vaginal ring, reiterate the importance of adherence and avoiding breaks in contraceptive use to avoid risk of pregnancy); educate patients on the importance of getting regular women's health and sexual/reproductive health checks. Encourage patients with concerns about the type of hormonal contraception they are using to speak with their medical practitioner or health service and make appropriate referrals. Discuss LARCs with patients when appropriate, as per RANZCOG recommendations.

provenance.section_heading: Provision of non-pharmacological and women's health advice

steps.description: Sexual health promotion and screening advice: condoms, when used correctly and consistently, are safe and highly effective in preventing transmission of most STIs (including HIV) and in reducing the risk of unplanned pregnancy; condoms are safe, inexpensive, and widely available. 'If the patient may be at increased risk of HIV and other STIs, pharmacists should advise them to seek review from their GP or a sexual health service for further assessment, testing, and discussion of HIV and STI prevention options.' Offer preventative healthcare referrals/education: cervical screening - routine screening available from age 25, recommended every five years; breast checks - personal or family history of breast cancer: advise seeing medical practitioner or health service; breast screening available for all women from age 40 (actively invited from age 50); STI screening as indicated.

gates.criterion: Patient not at increased risk of HIV and other STIs (if at increased risk, advise seek review from GP or sexual health service)

steps.description: Documentation and communication: 'The pharmacist must make an electronic clinical record, and a record in a pharmacy dispensing system regarding the supply of any medications under these services, in accordance with the Authority.' Where a patient has a My Health Record, the pharmacist must ensure the details of the supply are uploaded to My Health Record, unless requested otherwise by the patient. The pharmacist must share a copy of the record of the service with the patient and, if the patient consents, with the patient's usual treating medical practitioner or medical practice, where the patient has one, within a week following the consultation. Consultations and outcomes must be recorded using secure digital software; records must be stored securely for minimum seven (7) years. BP should be monitored and recorded every 12 months.

gates.criterion: Electronic clinical record and pharmacy dispensing system record made for the supply
Copy of the service record shared with the patient (and with usual treating medical practitioner/medical practice if the patient consents) within a week following the consultation

'Any changes in vaginal bleeding and the development or accompaniment of other symptoms may indicate underlying pathology. This requires referral to a medical practitioner or health service for further investigation and management.' Changes in bleeding pattern may include abnormalities in frequency (e.g. heavy bleeding), irregular bleeding, prolonged menstrual bleeding, abnormalities in volume, intermenstrual bleeding, and post-coital bleeding; accompanying symptoms may include dysmenorrhea, vaginal discharge, dyspareunia, changes in bladder or bowel function, weight gain or loss, headaches, visual disturbances, hirsutism, and acne.

'However, if the patient has not been using the method reliably and consistently and has had unprotected sex, then there is a risk of pregnancy. Pharmacists should take all reasonable steps and assessment to exclude pregnancy before continuation of hormonal contraception. Otherwise, the patient should be referred to a medical practitioner (or other authorised prescribing health practitioner) for assessment, pregnancy testing, and advice regarding ongoing contraception.'

open_questions.topic: Patient Assessment Flowchart (section D) not machine-readable
open_questions.observed: Pages 4 and 5 contain only 'D. PATIENT ASSESSMENT FLOWCHART', the introductory sentence and 'Page 4/5 of 19' - the flowchart itself is an image with no extractable text.
open_questions.why_unclear: The flowchart is described as the instrument that should 'assess the eligibility, identity and govern supply of suitable treatments, and guide associated referral requirements', but its decision nodes, gates and branches cannot be transcribed from the text extraction. PW-1 was reconstructed from the narrative sections (E, F, G, H); flowchart-specific branches may differ.

open_questions.topic: Ethinylestradiol strength unit printed as '35 g'
open_questions.observed: 'a. ethinylestadiol (35 g or less)' followed by a stray 'mu' character on the next line of the extraction; Table 1 headers use '(micrograms)' and list ethinylestradiol 20/30/35.
open_questions.why_unclear: The printed unit reads 'g' where micrograms are almost certainly intended (with a displaced mu symbol). Transcribed exactly as printed; not normalised.

open_questions.topic: Table 1 rows partially misaligned in text extraction
open_questions.observed: Rows such as 'drospirenone 3000 Bella, Brooke, Rosie, Yana, Yaz' and 'drospirenone 3000 Brooklynn, Isabelle, Petibelle, Rosalee, Yasmin, Yelena' have no estrogen column value; 'estetrol 14200 (14.2 mg) drospirenone 3000 Nextstellis' reads oddly; the Triphasic section prints Phase 1 (6 pills) and Phase 3 (10 pills) with no Phase 2 row; 'Seasonique [NB2]' appears as a stray line under the ethinylestradiol 30 + levonorgestrel 150 row.
open_questions.why_unclear: Table extraction is imperfect; estrogen-progestogen pairings for these rows cannot be confirmed from the text. Confidence marked unclear where relevant (TX-4).

open_questions.observed: 'ethinylestradiol 20 [NB1]', 'ethinylestradiol 30 [NB1]', 'Seasonique [NB2]' are printed but no corresponding NB1/NB2 footnote definitions appear in the extracted text.
open_questions.why_unclear: The meaning of the NB1/NB2 markers (likely formulation/strength caveats) is not printed in extractable text.

open_questions.topic: No general numeric age bounds printed
open_questions.observed: age_bounds left null/null. Method-specific ages appear instead: DMPA continuation 'aged 25 to 39 years old (inclusive) only'; footnote for patients aged 40-49 (one pack only); cervical screening from age 25; breast screening from age 40/invited from 50; 'Women over 35 who smoke', 'Women over 50'.
open_questions.why_unclear: The document states no minimum or maximum age for the continuation service as a whole, so no numeric age bound can be attributed to the eligibility section.

open_questions.observed: No regulation, poisons schedule provision or delegate instrument is cited; the document references 'the NSW Health Authority (25 February 2026)' and approval by the Chief Health Officer on 25 February 2026.
open_questions.why_unclear: The provision under which pharmacists may continue supply cannot be determined from the document text.

open_questions.topic: Eligibility combinatorics across service-wide and DMPA-specific groups
open_questions.observed: Service-wide requirements (INC-1..INC-6, INC-10) and DMPA-specific requirements (INC-7..INC-9) are printed as separate bullet groups; the document does not state explicit AND/OR combinatorics between them.
open_questions.why_unclear: Defaulted to all_of within each group; DMPA group members apply only when DMPA is the method being continued (per 'Continuation of DMPA under this service is permitted for...'). Cross-group combinatorics are not stated in the document.

open_questions.topic: Blood pressure referral threshold not quantified
open_questions.observed: 'If BP remains elevated, the patient should be referred...' - no numeric threshold or definition of 'elevated' is printed; a second reading is required at the end of the consultation.
open_questions.why_unclear: RF-6 and PW-1-S5 gate captured as qualitative (structured: null) because no value/units are given.

open_questions.topic: Genitourinary symptoms suggesting STI - no stated action
open_questions.observed: 'Presence of genitourinary symptoms that might suggest a STI: changes in vaginal or urethral discharge; vulval, genital skin problems or symptoms; lower abdominal pain; dysuria.' No referral, testing or escalation action is stated alongside these symptoms.
open_questions.why_unclear: RF-17 action REVIEW_GP is the nearest document-supported action (STI testing recommended for at-risk individuals; risk → seek review from GP or sexual health service), but the document does not state an action for symptomatic patients; confidence marked unclear.

open_questions.observed: The document lists referral destinations/criteria in scattered statements but never categorises them as routine, urgent or emergency; no emergency referral destination is printed.
open_questions.why_unclear: referral.routine/urgent assembled from quoted statements (first provenance page 6, statements span pages 6-13); referral.emergency left empty because the document specifies none.

open_questions.observed: PW-1-S3 'Sufficient information obtained', PW-1-S3 continuous-use/pill-break gate, PW-1-S4 genitourinary-symptoms gate, PW-1-S5 BMI measurement gate and PW-1-S12 record-sharing gate have on_fail 'unclear' because the document states the requirement but not the failure consequence.
open_questions.why_unclear: Spec requires 'unclear' plus an open question where the document does not state the branch action.

open_questions.observed: The document never ranks formulations or brands as first-line; it is a continuation (resupply) service and 'pharmacists are not permitted to initiate or change therapy'.
open_questions.why_unclear: first_line set to false for all treatment rows because the document makes no first-line designation.

open_questions.topic: Interaction of 12-month continuation allowance with the aged 40-49 single-pack limit
open_questions.observed: 'Pharmacists can provide continuation up to 12-months...' versus footnote 'For patients aged 40-49: pharmacists can only provide one original manufacturer's pack (only one resupply is allowed before the patient will need to be reviewed by their GP or other authorising prescribing healthcare practitioner).'
open_questions.why_unclear: How the single-pack rule for ages 40-49 reconciles with the general 12-month continuation supply is not explained (may be pack-size dependent).

open_questions.topic: Definition of 'continuation' for patients not on continuous therapy
open_questions.observed: 'Pharmacists must ascertain whether use of hormonal contraception has been continuous and can provide continuation according to the Practice Standard.' and 'If a patient frequently takes pill breaks, pharmacists should use professional judgement and consider referring the patient...'
open_questions.why_unclear: The document does not define how many pill breaks or what gap makes a patient ineligible; left to professional judgement.

open_questions.observed: TGA adverse-event reporting via https://aems.tga.gov.au/ and notification of the patient's usual GP are required 'Additionally'; no notifiable-condition or AIR notification is mentioned.
open_questions.why_unclear: notifiable.required set true on the basis of the adverse-event/GP/My Health Record notification statements; no notifiable disease condition is covered by the document.
